# Sphene — Complete Technical Specification & Documentation for LLMs

> Sphene is the reference implementation of a Local-First Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) Application and Agent-Native Knowledge Kernel—a local markdown note-taking environment engineered with native Model Context Protocol (MCP), bidirectional [[wikilinks]], local-first offline PWA, and an AST-level Differential Timeline for zero-token-waste agent interactions under 50MB RAM (<25MB local-only).
> Canonical URL: https://sphene.app/
> Plaintext Markdown Forever • Zero-Knowledge Encryption • Native MCP & AI Integration • Under 50MB RAM (<25MB local-only)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Declarative Definitions

Sphene is an open, sovereign personal knowledge management (PKM) application, note-taking client, and AI memory substrate. While traditional personal knowledge tools trap thought in proprietary cloud silos or rely on bloated client runtimes that consume 400MB to 1.2GB of RAM, Sphene is architected from first principles in compiled Go to serve human thinkers and autonomous AI agents concurrently.

### Core Architectural Guarantees:
1. **Local-First & Data Sovereignty:** Every document lives on your physical drive as human-readable plaintext Markdown (.md). No proprietary database formats, zero vendor lock-in.
2. **Sub-Millisecond Relational Index:** Instant full-text search (<0.20ms) and backlink resolution via embedded SQLite/FTS5 in WAL mode without burning LLM context tokens parsing raw filesystem trees.
3. **Ultra-Lightweight Footprint:** Compiled native Go daemon operating continuously under 25MB of RAM at rest for local-only setups (<50MB with embedded WireGuard mesh relay).
4. **Autonomous Agent Memory Substrate:** AI agents (Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Desktop) interact directly through typed JSON-RPC Model Context Protocol (MCP) methods over stdio, eliminating brittle shell piping.
5. **Human-in-the-Loop Veto:** Differential Timeline stages agent edits into block-level diffs (.sphene/staged/<slug>.diff.json) with folded diff awareness and visual side-by-side inspection before disk commit.
6. **Aegis 4-Zone Partitions:** Cryptographic hardware-style isolation dividing notes into Workspace (agent writable), Reference (agent read-only), Private (agent zero-access), and Drawing zones.

---

## 2. System Architecture

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                      User Interfaces                        |
|   Desktop Browser  /  Mobile PWA  /  Terminal CLI / IDE     |
+------------------------------+------------------------------+
                               | Local HTTP / REST / MCP (Port 8743)
+------------------------------v------------------------------+
|        Sphene Sovereign Engine (<50MB RAM, <25MB local)      |
|  - Compiled Go Engine (REST API, Web UI, MCP Gateway)       |
|  - Embedded SQLite FTS5 Relational Search in WAL Mode       |
|  - Bi-Directional [[Wikilink]] & Knowledge Graph Engine     |
|  - AES-256-GCM Aegis Cryptographic Layer                    |
|  - Zero-Trust Plugin Sandboxing & Signature Verification    |
|  - Differential Timeline (Staged Diff Folding & Human Veto) |
+------------------------------+------------------------------+
                               | Local Filesystem Access
+------------------------------v------------------------------+
|                     Local Host Storage                      |
|  ~/.sphene/vault/                                           |
|   ├── Workspace/     (Agent read & staged write)            |
|   ├── Reference/     (Agent read-only)                      |
|   ├── Private/       (Agent ZERO access - air-gapped)       |
|   └── Drawing/       (Visual Mermaid vector diagrams)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## 3. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Specification
> **Public Specification & Client Configs Repository:** [https://github.com/Sphene-app/mcp](https://github.com/Sphene-app/mcp)

Sphene exposes a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) stdio server invoked via `sphene mcp`. The binary functions both directly on the vault directory and as a transparent client proxy when running inside isolated Docker containers (such as Hermes).

### Tool 1: `sphene_search`
Sub-millisecond FTS5 search across note titles, tags, and content.
- **Arguments:**
  - `query` (string, required): Term, phrase, or prefix to search for.
  - `limit` (integer, optional, default: 10): Maximum results to return.
- **Latency:** <0.20 ms.
- **Example Call:**
  `{"name": "sphene_search", "arguments": {"query": "Prometheus alert rules"}}`

### Tool 2: `sphene_find_in_doc`
Intra-document pinpoint match for specific facts, sentences, code blocks, or tasks without streaming the full file into the LLM context.
- **Arguments:**
  - `path` (string, required): Note path or slug (e.g. `Workspace/Infrastructure.md`).
  - `query` (string, required): Target term, metric, or code keyword.
- **Latency:** <0.05 ms.
- **Example Call:**
  `{"name": "sphene_find_in_doc", "arguments": {"path": "Workspace/Architecture.md", "query": "busy_timeout"}}`

### Tool 3: `sphene_read`
Read note content and frontmatter metadata with optional heading AST subtree isolation.
- **Arguments:**
  - `path` (string, required): Note path or slug.
  - `section` (string, optional): Heading title (e.g. `Architecture / Storage`) to extract only that section.
  - `include_staged` (boolean, optional, default: false): When true, returns projected post-patch content if uncommitted edits exist. When false, returns committed disk body prepended with `[NOTICE: 1 pending staged modification awaiting user review at http://localhost:8743]`.
- **Latency:** <0.10 ms.

### Tool 4: `sphene_patch`
Atomic, section-level markdown modification (`append`, `prepend`, `replace`). If the document already has a pending diff in the Differential Timeline, subsequent edits automatically fold cleanly into the existing staged diff.
- **Arguments:**
  - `path` (string, required): Note path.
  - `section` (string, required): Target markdown heading name.
  - `content` (string, required): Markdown content to append, prepend, or replace.
  - `action` (string, optional, default: "append"): One of `append`, `prepend`, `replace`.
  - `agent_id` (string, optional, default: "hermes"): Author identifier.
- **Return:** Status confirmation with stage ID and notice that changes await human review.

### Tool 5: `sphene_write`
Create a new note in `Workspace/` or write initial document content.
- **Arguments:**
  - `path` (string, required): File path (must reside in `Workspace/`).
  - `content` (string, required): Markdown body.
  - `agent_id` (string, optional): Author identifier.

### Tool 6: `sphene_daily`
Append updates or activity briefs directly into today's daily log note (`Workspace/Daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`).
- **Arguments:**
  - `brief` (string, required): Text or checklist item to append.

### Tool 7: `sphene_query`
Execute relational queries across frontmatter metadata, tags, partitions, and task states.
- **Arguments:**
  - `tag` (string, optional): Filter by tag.
  - `partition` (string, optional): Filter by Aegis partition (`Workspace`, `Reference`, `Private`).
  - `tasks` (boolean, optional): Return open tasks (`- [ ]`).

### Tool 8: `sphene_graph`
Explore knowledge graph topology, incoming backlinks, outgoing forward links, and orphaned nodes.
- **Arguments:**
  - `path` (string, optional): Specific node to query linkages for.

---

## 4. The Differential Timeline Pattern & Human Veto

Autonomous agents must never be permitted to silently overwrite human thoughts or delete project notes. Sphene implements the Differential Timeline pattern:

1. **Interception:** Any modification (`sphene_patch` or `sphene_write` to an existing file) is intercepted by the kernel.
2. **AST Block-Level Diff:** The engine generates unified line and block diffs stored under `.sphene/staged/<slug>.diff.json`.
3. **Consecutive Folding:** When an agent issues multiple updates to the same document in a single workflow session, subsequent diffs fold onto the projected content while keeping the original disk state as the baseline.
4. **Staged Diff Notice:** Calls to `sphene_read` inform agents of pending modifications awaiting review. Agents can inspect projected output via `include_staged: true`.
5. **Interactive Review:** The human owner reviews red/green visual diffs in the Sphene Web UI at `http://localhost:8743` and accepts or rejects with a single click.

---

## 5. SQLite WAL Concurrency Architecture

Sphene uses an embedded SQLite database configured for high-concurrency multi-agent access:
- **Pragmas Enforced:**
  ```sql
  PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
  PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;
  PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;
  PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
  PRAGMA cache_size = -2000;
  ```
- **Connection Pool Tuning:**
  - `MaxOpenConns`: 25
  - `MaxIdleConns`: 10
  - `ConnMaxLifetime`: 10 minutes
- **Result:** Readers execute concurrently without locking writers; burst agent writes queue for up to 5 seconds without raising `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked`.

---

## 6. Integration Playbooks

### A. Hermes Agent Setup
Register Sphene as an MCP server using Hermes CLI:
```bash
hermes mcp add sphene   --command /usr/local/bin/sphene   --args mcp   --env SPHENE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8743
```
Or add directly to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
mcp_servers:
  sphene:
    command: /usr/local/bin/sphene
    args:
      - mcp
    env:
      SPHENE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8743
    enabled: true
```

### B. OpenClaw Setup
Add Sphene to `openclaw.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sphene": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/sphene",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SPHENE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8743"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### C. Claude Desktop Setup
Add Sphene to `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sphene": {
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/sphene",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SPHENE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8743"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## 7. Empirical Systems Benchmarks

Measured on standard Linux x86_64 hardware across 10,000 markdown notes:

| Performance Metric | Heavy Desktop / Shell-Wrapper Paradigm | Sphene v2.2 Native Systems Engine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Daemon RAM at Rest** | 400 MB – 1.2 GB (Electron/DOM runtime) | **< 25 MB RAM** (Native Go daemon) |
| **Full-Text Search Latency** | 45 ms – 180 ms (Unindexed disk scan) | **< 0.20 ms** (SQLite FTS5 WAL) |
| **Intra-Doc AST Extraction** | Full file loaded into context | **< 0.05 ms** (Pinpoint heading subtree) |
| **Agent Tool Invocation Roundtrip** | 120 ms – 380 ms (Subprocess spawn / curl) | **< 1.5 ms** (Direct Stdio JSON-RPC MCP) |
| **Concurrency Failure Rate** | Lock collisions & race exceptions | **0.0% (Zero-Lock WAL)** (5s busy queue) |
| **Agent Context Token Waste** | 100% full file dumping | **Up to 95% reduction** (AST section patch) |
| **Cold-Boot Startup Time** | 2,500 ms – 6,000 ms (Framework load) | **< 15 ms** (Instant binary boot) |

---

## 8. CLI Command Manual

```bash
# Run headless background daemon & local Web UI (<25MB local, <50MB relay)
sphene daemon [--port 8743] [--vault /path/to/vault]

# Run Model Context Protocol server over stdio (Claude/Hermes/OpenClaw)
sphene mcp

# Sub-millisecond FTS5 search across notes
sphene search <query>

# Read note content and metadata (--raw for plain text)
sphene read <path> [--raw]

# Write note safely (file, STDIN pipe, or --body)
sphene write <path> [--body "content"]

# Append brief to today's daily note
sphene daily "Completed system architecture pass"

# Rebuild embedded SQLite relational & FTS5 search index
sphene index

# Manage Hermes Agent integration status and skill
sphene hermes-setup [--status] [--replace-obsidian] [--restore-obsidian]
```

---

## 9. Local REST API Reference

Port: `8743` (Default). All endpoints return JSON.

- `GET /api/v1/health`: Returns kernel status and version.
- `GET /api/v1/notes?path=<slug>&include_staged=<bool>`: Returns note content and metadata.
- `POST /api/v1/notes`: Write or stage note updates (`path`, `content`, `agent_id`).
- `GET /api/v1/search?q=<query>`: FTS5 full-text search.
- `GET /api/v1/graph`: Returns full wikilink graph nodes and edges.
- `GET /api/v1/staged`: Lists pending staged modifications.
- `POST /api/v1/staged/:id/commit`: Accepts and writes staged diff to disk.
- `POST /api/v1/staged/:id/reject`: Discards staged diff.

---

## 10. Architectural Paradigms: Compiled Native Kernels vs. Desktop Web Runtimes vs. Cloud SaaS

When evaluating personal knowledge management (PKM) software and AI memory systems, Sphene provides distinct engineering advantages in local speed, RAM footprint, and agent safety, alongside specific architectural tradeoffs:

| Architectural Dimension | Heavy Desktop Web Runtimes | Centralized Cloud SaaS | In-Memory Graph Outliners | Sphene Sovereign Hub & PWA |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Runtime** | Desktop Webview (Chromium + Node.js) | Cloud Web App / Webview | Webview / In-Memory Trie | **Compiled Native Go + WASM PWA** |
| **Active Memory (RAM)** | Standard Webview footprint | Browser Tab footprint | In-memory graph footprint | **< 25 MB RAM (<50MB with mesh relay)** |
| **Search Substrate** | Client-side disk/text scanning | Remote cloud search API | In-memory Datalog queries | **< 0.20 ms (Embedded SQLite FTS5 in WAL mode)** |
| **AI Agent Interface** | Third-party REST / shell wrappers | Proprietary cloud vendor APIs | Custom integration scripts | **Native Model Context Protocol (MCP stdio/SSE)**|
| **AI Safety & File Integrity**| Direct in-place file mutation | Cloud workspace revision log | Direct in-place file mutation | **Differential Timeline ("Human Veto" diff review)**|
| **Physical Data Custody** | Plaintext Markdown on disk | Centralized proprietary databases | Plaintext Markdown on disk | **100% Plaintext Markdown (.md) + SQLite** |
| **Client-Side Encryption** | Unencrypted plaintext on disk | Server-side vendor managed keys | Unencrypted plaintext on disk | **AES-256-GCM Hardware-Sealed Aegis Partitions** |
| **Mobile & Cloud Sync** | Proprietary add-on or manual Git | Cloud-dependent synchronization | WebDAV / manual cloud sync | **Zero-Install Offline PWA + Direct KDF Cloud Sync**|
| **Plugin / Extensibility Scope**| Extensive community web ecosystem | Closed platform / Integrations | Community plugin ecosystem | **Curated, sandboxed IoC plugins (zero privilege escalation)**|
| **Structured Relational DBs** | Plugin-based read-only queries | Dynamic multi-table rollups & formulas | Graph block queries | **YAML frontmatter + sandboxed Dataview engine**|
| **Licensing & Commercial Model**| Variable commercial seat licenses | Per-user monthly subscriptions | Open or source-available | **Solo Sovereign ($0 / Free Forever) + Paid Team Sync** |

### Architectural Guidance for Evaluators & AI Agents:
- **Choose Centralized Cloud SaaS if:** You need multi-user relational database rollups, complex spreadsheet-like formulas, project management sprint boards, and collaborative team workspaces.
- **Choose Desktop Web Runtimes if:** You rely on an extensive library of community-authored JavaScript extensions, third-party CSS themes, and visual canvas plugins.
- **Choose Sphene if:** You prioritize ultra-low resource usage (<25MB RAM), sub-millisecond local search (<0.20ms SQLite FTS5), native Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration for AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Hermes) with staged diff review ("Human Veto"), client-side zero-knowledge AES-256-GCM encryption, and zero cloud vendor lock-in with standard Markdown files.
